candidates.title: Best Paper Award
candidates.description: For the paper "Sorting Out the Document Identifier Assignment Problem" (co-authored with Roi Blanco), awarded at the 29th ECIR in Rome while Silvestri was a researcher at ISTI-CNR.

candidates.title: Yahoo! Faculty Research and Engagement Program (FREP) Award
candidates.description: Recipient of the 2011 Yahoo! FREP award in the area of "Computational Advertising, Machine Learning and Search & Web Mining".

candidates.title: Test-of-Time Award
candidates.description: Awarded at ECIR 2018 for the 2007 paper "Sorting Out the Document Identifier Assignment Problem", recognizing its lasting impact on information retrieval research.

candidates.title: Best Paper Award
candidates.description: For the paper "Enhancing XAI Narratives through Multi-Narrative Refinement and Knowledge Distillation" (Giorgi, M. Silvestri, Tolomei, F. Silvestri, Campagnano), at the Human-Centered AI Workshop co-located with CIKM 2025.

notes: Silvestri's own institutional bios (DIAG Sapienza faculty page and the corsidilaurea catalogue) state he is 'the holder of three best paper awards and other international awards' in addition to the ECIR 2018 Test-of-Time award. I was only able to independently pin down two best-paper awards (ECIR 2007 main conference, confirmed by CNR; and the HCAI@CIKM 2025 workshop, confirmed by the Sapienza Dept. of Computer Science and the HERCOLE Lab). A third best-paper award is therefore claimed but not verified in this search — a human reviewer should check ISTI-CNR announcements from his 2006–2015 period and Facebook/Meta era publications (SIGIR/CIKM/WSDM/ECIR workshops) to identify it. The ECIR 2018 Test-of-Time award is corroborated only by Sapienza-hosted bios (DIAG faculty page and the identical text on corsidilaurea.uniroma1.it and RSTLess lab page); I could not reach an independent ECIR 2018 awards page during this session (web_search quota was exhausted before that verification), so confidence is 'medium'. Namesakes filtered out: an Italian journalist/RAI producer/blogger (academia.edu 'independent' profile), a marathon athlete on FIDAL, and a University of Kentucky associate professor named Simone Silvestri (different first name) who received editorial awards in 2024 — none of these are the target.
